concept.name: Overnight session
concept.definition: Trading that occurs outside a market's daytime session, spanning the evening, night, and early morning; in U.S.-based futures markets, the overnight session on CME Globex runs from the evening open (e.g., 6:30 p.m. ET) through to the next day's close, encompassing Asian and European hours.
concept.intuition: Futures markets barely sleep: after the U.S. day ends, trading hands off to Asia and Europe before the next U.S. morning.
concept.mechanics: Electronic venues like CME Globex operate near-24-hour schedules with a daily maintenance break; activity is commonly described by regional sessions (Asia, London, U.S.), and the overnight session establishes the price levels at which the daytime session will open.
concept.failure_modes: Overnight liquidity is thinner and headline-sensitive — weekend gaps and overnight spikes can be sharp, and risk limits sized for daytime volatility can be breached while staffing is minimal.
concept.misconceptions: The overnight session is not a separate market with separate prices — it is the same continuous contract — but its price action still belongs to the same or next trade date, which confuses P&L and chart construction.
concept.example: E-mini S&P 500 futures reopen at 6:00 p.m. ET Sunday on CME Globex; the overnight session trades through Asian and European hours before U.S. equity markets open Monday at 9:30 a.m.

citations.source: CME Group, Trading Hours (BrokerTec U.S. Actives on CME Globex)
citations.section: Normal hours of operation (evening open to next-day close); Asia/London/U.S. session hours
